ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Korea's AML/CFT legal framework is governed by the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10409, as amended), the Act on Real Name Confirmation Under Financial Transactions, the Financial Services Commission's Regulation on Customer Identification, the Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 8422, as amended) for Yuhan Hoesa registration and corporate governance, the Framework Act on National Taxes and Local Tax Act for registration and taxation, and the Korean Commercial Registration Rules; the Republic of Korea's implementation of FATF Recommendations and UN Security Council Resolutions regarding terrorist financing is administered by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Corporate Register Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the District Court / Supreme Court Commercial Registration System (I-REG), Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an apostille destination: notarize the certified extract, then affix a Hague Apostille through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). For a non-apostille destination: notarize, have the extract certified by MOFA, and then obtain consular legalization from the destination country's Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. Use one path only; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Business Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an apostille destination: notarize the certificate and obtain a Hague Apostille from MOFA. For a non-apostille destination: notarize, obtain MOFA authentication, then complete consular legalization at the destination country's Embassy or Consulate in Korea. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (Authorizing Incorporation and Banking Signatures)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Founding Entity, notarized by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the board resolution and power of attorney; then choose either (a) Hague Apostille by MOFA for Apostille Convention states or (b) MOFA authentication followed by consular legalization by the destination state's Embassy/Consulate for non-member states. Never apply both paths to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators/Founder Representatives, notarized by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original Articles of Association are notarized; if the destination requires apostille, proceed directly with Hague Apostille by MOFA. If the destination is not an Apostille state, proceed through MOFA authentication and then consular legalization by the destination country's diplomatic mission. These are alternative authentication chains, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Corporate Banking Account Subsistence and AML/CFT Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean Commercial Bank (Corporate Banking Center)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is signed and sealed by the bank's authorized officer; for use in apostille jurisdictions, attach a notarized certification and obtain MOFA Hague Apostille. For non-apostille jurisdictions, after notarization and MOFA authentication, obtain consular legalization from the destination country's Embassy or Consulate in Korea. One path only must be selected.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, beneficial shareholders, and signatories against (i) the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions list and UN SCR 1373; (ii) US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list and country-sanctioned jurisdictions; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the UK HMT sanctioned persons list; (v) the Republic of Korea's own unilateral sanctions and designated list administered by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission; and (vi) all applicable PRC lists only to the extent a Chinese UBO is involved. The screening must be performed prior to any engagement, repeated every 24 hours during formation, and with negative-news/PEP determination under a risk-based approach. All hits, negative matches, and PEP relationships must be escalated to the compliance committee and, if required, to KoFIU; no formation may proceed until the Enhanced Due Diligence file is cleared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-REG) Online Name Reservation and Duplicate-Check Service of the Supreme Court of Korea (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean trade name must be expressed in Hangul or a permissible combination incorporating Latin uppercase letters, Arabic numerals, Hangul phonetic transliteration, and limited symbols; it must end with the Korean legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign words must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul for the registered Korean name, while a parallel English name may be registered separately. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) distinctive brand element, (2) business-scope descriptor, (3) legal-form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa', and (4) a unique serialized or trademark-consistent identifier. Chinese characters are not permitted as a primary registered trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a name application, the applicant receives a written refusal stating the grounds. The applicant may file a corrective re-application with a revised name through I-REG, or submit a written objection to the Head of the relevant Registry Office under the Commercial Act and Administrative Appeal Act. The objection must set out the legal basis, evidence of distinctiveness, prior trademark or trade-name searches, and a request for ministerial approval where the refused token is sensitive. The registry must respond within 60 days. Reservations expire after six months and are not formally extended; a new reservation application must be filed before expiry to maintain priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mail-forwarding virtual office is generally rejected by Korean banks and the National Tax Service because it lacks physical facilities for corporate substance. For a low-risk webnovel subscription platform, a serviced-office model with a dedicated professional address, lease agreement, physical signage, and administrative staff is permissible if the registered address is not merely a virtual mailbox. Korean AML customer due diligence requires a verifiable registered office matching the corporate registry, with evidence of lease contracts, utility bills, or tax receipts. Tax authorities may treat a mailbox-only office as a sham office and deny business registration or VAT deductions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk is low for this low-risk LLC, quantified at approximately 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first operating year absent red flags. Checklist: (1) display the registered trade-name sign at the office entrance; (2) maintain a current lease contract, security deposit receipts, utility bills, and VAT registration certificate; (3) keep board resolutions, capital funding records, and minute books; (4) ensure director or authorized staff are present during normal business hours; (5) reconcile Apple IAP and Google Play Billing revenue records with the registered business description; and (6) maintain corporate seal and registration documents on site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, promulgated January 27, 1962, as most recently amended; Chapter IV, Articles 543 et seq. governing Yuhan Hoesa limited companies), together with the Company Registration Rules of the Supreme Court of Korea; specifically the provisions on articles of association, contribution subscription, contribution payment, statutory deposit, officer appointment, and registration of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division, District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, supervised by the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea (and, for electronic filing, the Korean Court E-Registration Portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Supreme Court Company Registration Rules, submitted together with the notarized Articles of Association, contribution deposit certificate, and officer acceptance statements.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under Korean law a Yuhan Hoesa does not have a statutory minimum paid-up capital; the incorporated capital is the total amount stated in the notarized Articles of Association, divided into contribution units. All cash contributions must be actually paid into a blocked contribution-protection account at a domestic bank or entrusted to a notary public before the incorporation application is filed, and the deposit must remain blocked until the company is registered. Non-cash contributions must be fully described in the Articles and supported by an independent appraisal where required. There is no separate escrow beyond this statutory blocked-deposit requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Resolution of the Board of Managing Directors of [●] Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Company). At a duly convened meeting of the Board of Managing Directors of the Company held at [●], Republic of Korea, on [●] at [●] a.m. KST, the following directors were present in person and constituted a valid quorum under the Articles of Association: [●]. The meeting was chaired by [●]. Conscious of their fiduciary duties under the Korean Commercial Act, the directors resolved as follows: 1. Share capital subscription and contribution. The notarized Articles of Association, the subscription register, and the contribution deposit certificate issued by [●] Bank were reviewed. The total registered capital of the Company is [●] Korean Won, divided into [●] contribution units of [●] Korean Won each. The directors accept the subscriptions recorded in the register and direct that all cash contributions remain in the blocked contribution-protection account until the District Court Registry effects incorporation registration. In respect of each subscriber, the liability of that member is limited to the unpaid portion of his or her contribution, if any, to the extent permitted by the Korean Commercial Act. 2. Adoption of registered office. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [●], [●]-gu, [●] City, Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to execute and perform the lease, to obtain the landlord written consent and floor plan, and to use that office as the legal seat for service of process, official notices, and corporate records. 3. Banking authorization. The Representative Director and [●] are authorized to open corporate current and settlement accounts with [●] Bank, to register the corporate seal, to sign account mandates, and to receive, hold, and disburse subscription income and settlement proceeds from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing solely through such accounts. 4. Statutory officer appointments. The following persons are appointed for the first statutory term: [●] as Representative Director and President; [●] as Financial Director and Chief Compliance Officer; and [●] as Data Protection Officer. Each appointee has accepted the office, is not disqualified under the Commercial Act, and is lawfully capable of acting. 5. Execution and ratification. The Representative Director is directed to file the incorporation application at the District Court Registry, to obtain the Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service, to appoint external legal counsel and independent accountants, and to perform all routine acts necessary to make the Company operational. All previous acts undertaken in good faith for the benefit of the Company are hereby ratified. This resolution is immediately effective and shall remain in full force until revoked or modified by a later valid resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, Execute, and Notarize the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public accredited under the Korean Notarial Association / Ministry of Justice, in the district where the registered office of the Yuhan Hoesa will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Korean-qualified attorney to prepare the Korean-language Articles of Association for the Yuhan Hoesa. The document must state the corporate purpose, which is the operation of a serialized digital web-fiction and interactive reading application platform; the corporate name; the address of the registered office; the total registered capital and the number and nominal value of contribution units; the method of contribution; director tenure; meeting rules; and method of public announcement. All incorporators, or their duly notarized attorneys-in-fact, must appear before the notary public, prove their identity, sign or seal the Articles of Association, and receive the notary certificate. Certified copies must be retained for the later court registration. If a foreign incorporator signs by proxy, an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney should be attached.
required_dossiers: Draft Korean-language Articles of Association
Identity documents of each incorporator (passport or Alien Registration Card)
Power of attorney, if any, apostilled and translated into Korean
Personal seal certificate or notarized seal impression of each incorporator
Notarial fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the purpose clause as too broad, revise the purpose to describe expressly the digital web-fiction and mobile application services; if a foreign incorporator lacks the proper certificate, obtain a certified apostille and exact Korean translation; if the notary requires changes, re-print and re-sign all copies before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Contributions into Blocked Contribution-Protection Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic Korean commercial bank branch or notary public designated under the Korean Commercial Act as contribution depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Articles are notarized, the Representative Director or a founding subscriber must open a temporary contribution-protection account in the name of the company being incorporated, or in the name of the subscriber as trustee for the company, at a domestic Korean bank. Each subscriber must transfer the exact amount of his or her cash contribution into the account and ensure that the name on the deposit matches the subscriber register. The bank will issue a contribution deposit certificate or passbook entry specifically stating that the funds are for incorporation of [●] Yuhan Hoesa and are blocked until registration. If any contribution is in kind, secure an independent valuation report and attach a description of the property to the notarized Articles. Funds cannot be withdrawn or pledged before registration. After court registration, the blocked account may be released to the company operating account.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of contribution deposit issued in the corporate name
Account opening confirmation or passbook copy
Subscriber ledger and amounts reconciled with the Articles
Independent valuation report for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account because the company is not yet registered, use a subscriber or trustee account with full beneficial-owner disclosure; if the deposit certificate lacks blocked-language, request the bank to amend the certificate; if funds are withdrawn by mistake, return the exact amount and redeposit with clear reference to the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration Application with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Division, District Court Registry Office with jurisdiction over the registered office, accessible physically or through the Korean Court E-Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard application for registration of incorporation and pay the court registration fee, computed at the statutory rate of 0.4 percent of capital plus the local education surcharge of 0.2 percent of capital. Attach the notarized Articles of Association, the contribution deposit certificate, the written acceptance of each director, the written consent of the owner or lessor for the registered office, and the lease agreement or ownership document. If a non-resident is named as director, supply a domestic service address or evidence of an appointed process agent. File within the statutory period after subscription and payment are completed, and submit the corporate seal impression. The registry will examine whether the articles are notarized and whether the capital has been paid. Upon completion, the registry will issue the certificate of registered matters, which is conclusive proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank certificate of contribution deposit
Written acceptance of each director
Registered office lease and landlord consent or ownership certificate
Power of attorney if filed by counsel
Corporate seal and seal impression card
Receipt of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, provide the curative document, such as amended articles, corrected deposit certificate, or landlord consent, within the given period; if the application is rejected, request a written explanation and file an immediate appeal to the competent district court within two weeks of receipt; registration fees may be refunded or applied to resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Corporate Seal and Obtain Business Registration Certificate from the Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office or the Main Office Tax Office designated by the National Tax Service serving the registered office address, together with the Hometax e-filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of registered matters, deliver the corporate seal to the designated tax office and register the seal impression for tax invoices and documentary contracts. Complete the Application for Business Registration and submit it within twenty calendar days of the effective incorporation date to the tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must identify the business as an online digital content publishing and electronic subscription platform service under the appropriate tax classification and must state the representative director, the place of business, and the bank account. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate and assign the corporate number. The company should then activate electronic tax invoice issuance, register the open bank account, and confirm the corporate VAT and corporate tax filing periods. This certificate is necessary for contracts and for the Apple and Google developer account settlement process.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters
Corporate seal registration application and seal impression
Lease agreement with landlord consent and building ownership certificate
Identification of the Representative Director
Application for Business Registration
Proof of paid-in capital deposit or initial financial statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional proof of the place of business, obtain from the landlord a current certified copy of the building register and a written lease; if the tax office disagrees with the business classification, file an amended business registration with the correct online publishing code; if the certificate is delayed, request a temporary registration certificate and continue operational onboarding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Accounts and Onboard International Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Korean depository institution, Apple Developer Program / App Store Connect, and Google Play Console, using the company corporate registration and tax certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a current operating account in the name of the Yuhan Hoesa using the certificate of registered matters, the Business Registration Certificate, the corporate seal, and director identification. Instruct the bank to release the blocked contribution-protection balance to the operating account after incorporation. Apply to Apple and Google to register the developer entity, provide the Business Registration Certificate and bank settlement documents, and designate Apple IAP and Google Play Billing as the in-app payment rails. A merchant or settlement agreement may be required, and the corporate banking authorization resolution must be submitted. This step is performed only after the company exists as a legal entity and enables the platform to collect subscription revenue through compliant payment channels.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal and seal certificate
Board resolution authorizing bank accounts
Representative Director identification and Alien Registration Card if foreign
Bank account opening application and signature cards
Apple and Google developer entity forms and tax information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Apple or Google reject the entity because of a tax information mismatch, provide the Business Registration Certificate and ensure the legal name exactly matches the certificate; if the bank questions the blocked account release, provide the court registration certificate; if a payment processor requires additional corporate authority, provide a board resolution and re-submit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the entity is a pure digital web-fiction subscription platform; it operates no physical factory, chemical plant, assembly line, or warehouse and therefore no industrial licensing board authorizes its business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — there is no manufacturing or physical operating permit required for the operation of an online serialized web-novel reading application; the platform is a non-licensed digital content service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation have no EIA role where no physical installation is constructed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no project falls within EIA activation under the Framework Act on Environmental Policy or the Act on Assessment of Environmental Impact; only office use is contemplated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — the coded digital service generates no point-source wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound process emissions, or hazardous waste stream subject to quantitative Korean Clean Air Conservation Act or Water Quality Act limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial permit. If the company leases a general office, the landlord and the company shall maintain standard fire-fighting equipment and the building must have a lawful occupancy certificate under the Building Act, but no Civil Defense fire permit is required for the non-industrial software-only operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly formed Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) owned by non-resident shareholders, the resident representative must obtain a Business Registration Certificate (10-digit Korean TIN / VAT ID) by submitting an Application for Business Registration to the competent district tax office or via HomeTax using the accredited digital certificate. The filing must include: articles of incorporation and court registration certificate from the Korean commercial registration registry; certificate of foreign-investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for each non-resident shareholder; lease agreement or proof of a Korean office; copy of the representative's passport and alien registration card; corporate seal registration; and, if applicable, a power of attorney in favor of a certified tax accountant. The district tax office issues the Business Registration Certificate normally within five working days. The entity must then register for the electronic e-Tax Invoice system through HomeTax and obtain an API/ERP authorization for machine-to-machine e-invoice clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea operates a mandatory system-level entity classification; a Yuhan Hoesa is per se a domestic corporation under the Korean Commercial Act. No check-the-box election exists for domestic corporations. Hybrid mismatch adjustments may apply under the Corporate Tax Act and the Adjustment of International Transactions Act, but no ex-ante election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for corporate entities; a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC) must register regardless of turnover. Individual small businesses may use the simplified taxpayer regime if annual taxable sales do not exceed KRW 30,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax invoices) through HomeTax or via an NTS-certified ERP/API interface within one business day after the supply date. Each e-Tax invoice carries a mandatory digital signature from the supplier's HomeTax digital certificate, and the invoice data are transmitted to the NTS near-real-time for anti-fraud clearance and digital stamping. For business-to-consumer electronic commerce, including app-store subscription sales, the platform must integrate with the National HomeTax cash receipt API and issue electronic cash receipts when customers request them; non-issuance triggers statutory penalties. All sales ledgers and e-Tax invoice registries must be retained for the Korean statutory five-year tax record period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 24(1) of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, the supply of services to non-residents that are actually consumed in a foreign country qualifies for 0% VAT. For the web-novel subscription platform, all digital subscription fees received from overseas end-users through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are zero-rated when the platform holds conclusive evidence that the purchaser is a foreign non-obligated party, the content is delivered to a foreign IP/device, and the sales proceeds are remitted in foreign currency to the Korean entity's bank account. If the app-store settlement report identifies Korean users, the corresponding revenue is taxable at the standard 10% VAT rate and must be reported separately. The zero rate also applies to overseas digital-content royalties and licenses when the service is physically or electronically consumed outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration / export clearance confirmation - required only where the platform ships physical branded goods or media; for pure app-delivered digital web fiction an internal electronic dispatch ledger must be retained

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill - applicable only to physical ancillary exports; for digital app subscriptions the functional equivalent is the Apple App Store and Google Play settlement report evidencing digital delivery to foreign storefront accounts

Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, confirming repatriation of foreign sales proceeds
Apple IAP and Google Play Billing monthly vendor financial reports disclosing sales amounts by territory and currency
IP geolocation, storefront region, device locale, and user-account registration logs demonstrating that the subscription service is consumed outside Korea
Commercial invoices and service contracts identifying the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as the seller of exported digital subscription rights
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service perform risk-based audits on exported digital content. If the zero-rated supply is not substantiated with complete foreign-currency payment evidence within the 180-day repatriation window, the supply is reclassified as taxable domestic supply and the NTS will assess 10% VAT on the full base plus additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act for failure to issue or correct the tax invoice. For fraudulent or unverified zero-rating, the NTS may impose a penalty equal to 40% of the avoided VAT or of the falsely claimed export value, whichever is greater, and may also apply penalties for false e-Tax invoices. Any foreign exchange proceeds retained beyond 180 days without justifiable cause attract statutory default interest and may trigger separate penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. In addition, the NTS has a clawback mechanism that reverses the zero rate retroactively, adds statutory penalty surcharges, and can extend the audit period to the full statute of limitations for tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as monetary authority and central bank; under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Ministry of Economy and Finance is the principal foreign exchange regulatory body, with delegated reporting administration to the Bank of Korea, Korea Customs Service, and licensed foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade settlement, royalties, software license fees, and digital content subscription remittances, provided that underlying documentation and purpose codes are filed with the local authorized FX bank. Capital account convertibility is highly liberalized but not automatic: all capital injections, foreign currency loans, overseas remittances for M&A, and bond issuance require prior reporting or approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds; exporters may maintain foreign currency receipts in domestic foreign currency accounts indefinitely, and conversion to KRW is at the market rate. Profit remittance is permissible once corporate tax and dividend withholding tax (typically 20-22% on gross dividends, reduced under tax treaties) have been discharged; the bank will require audited financials, board approval of dividends, tax clearance certificates, and the foreign exchange purchase confirmation. The Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) requires banks to apply a real-demand rule for FX transactions, meaning all FX conversions and derivatives must correspond to genuine underlying cross-border business activity. In practice, digital content platforms with high micro-transaction velocity face enhanced scrutiny because small Apple/Google IAP settlements create many credits; banks must map these to the platform's revenue recognition and underlying author contracts. A Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with non-resident ownership must register the inward capital transfer under the Foreign Direct Investment procedure with a designated foreign exchange bank, obtain a capital verification certificate, and ensure that subsequent reimbursement of development costs or intercompany licensing fees does not breach the principle of 'one sale, one FX transaction' requiring a single underlying invoice. Overall, Korea does not impose surrender requirements or punitive remittance taxes; the main operational challenge is documentary traceability and meeting bank-specific foreign exchange declaration windows (typically 30 days for receipt and disbursement reporting).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 9 and related enforcement provisions of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds (including digital content and service earnings) must be received and collected within 6 months from the export date or service completion date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; exporters may retain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign currency deposit account or convert voluntarily. If the collection deadline cannot be met, the entity must file an extension application with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through its foreign exchange bank, with extensions granted up to an additional 2 years for bona fide commercial reasons. All receipts must be reported to the bank within the standard reporting timeline, and the bank must issue a foreign exchange purchase confirmation (매매확인증) for any conversion used for capital verification or tax documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. The Banking Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reserve cross-border FX brokerage and domestic KRW deposit-taking to licensed banks and licensed foreign exchange banks. Offshore digital EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, Airwallex, or Currencycloud are not legally permitted to open KRW current accounts or act as an FX intermediary for a Korean entity without obtaining a banking license from the Financial Services Commission (FSC). Using a fintech EMI issuer for Korean entity treasury would fail the capital verification requirement of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, expose the Yuhan Hoesa to unlicensed money transmission risk, and be rejected by the Financial Supervisory Service audit. EMIs may only support invoicing or payments in their home currency via local partner banks, which does not satisfy the 'authorized foreign exchange bank' status required for purposes of reporting inward direct investment, dividend remittance, or trade settlement. Therefore, all cross-border treasury flows must use the domestic tier-1 bank channels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with non-resident directors, all major Korean banks require a face-to-face KYC interview at the branch for at least one statutory director or designated officer. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for the first year of corporate banking relations. The acceptable alternative for remote onboarding is a notarized power of attorney, an apostilled director passport copy, a corporate certificate of good standing from the home jurisdiction, and a video interview with the bank's compliance manager. However, Shinhan Bank and KEB Hana Bank allow proxy opening after a documentary legalization review, with the foreign director physically present at the bank within 90 days to sign additional agreements. Woori Bank and KB Kookmin Bank insist on physical presence of the director at least once for the initial account opening. The bank compliance committee will also require original or certified copies of the Korean corporate registration (certificate of incorporation and business start-up tax reports), the LLC's articles of incorporation, and securities registration certificates for foreign-invested enterprises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Micro-transaction funding pattern: thousands of low-value credits from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing books into the company account without a clear per-payer economic rationale, which resembles money mule inflow or synthetic transaction layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the official Apple Developer Program payout statements and Google Play payout reports for the last 12 months; platform user growth demography and average order values; a detailed architecture of the subscription billing engine showing exact mapping from each app-store transaction to the internal subscriber ledger; an annual external IT audit certificate confirming that no user P2P transfer or escrow account is embedded in the app; and a written explanation of the chargeback/fraud policy, including positive customer identification and device binding records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to foreign authors and content studios: royalty flows to dozens of offshore beneficiaries could mask sanctions circumvention or impermissible transfers to prohibited jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a complete corporate IP register and licensing tree, including contracts with each content author, distribution agreements with Apple/Google, sub-licensing agreements for translated editions, beneficial ownership declarations for each foreign payee, current sanctions-screening and negative-news reports for each beneficiary, and the withholding tax certificates (Form 8802/W-8BEN-E or equivalent) matched to each royalty payment. In addition, provide a monthly royalty calculation spreadsheet showing the net amount after platform commission and tax withholding, and a bank confirmation from the recipient's financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign direct investment injection ambiguity: inbound remittance from a non-resident shareholder may be classified improperly as a loan instead of equity, creating distortions in capital verification and dividends.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the report of foreign direct investment (신고필증) stamped by the designated foreign exchange bank or MOTIE; the original remittance wire with purpose code 100010 (Foreign Direct Investment); the bank-issued foreign exchange purchase confirmation; the shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase; a copy of the board minutes authorizing the subscription of LLC units; and an independent valuation or accountants' certificate confirming the amount is fully paid into the escrow account under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual credit card / mobile billing abuse: in-app subscriptions could be sold on gray markets or used to launder proceeds from illegal websites through stolen payment instruments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the platform's formal anti-fraud and AML procedures, including real-name verification, device fingerprinting, velocity rules, IP geolocation flags; the SOC 2 Type II or equivalent vendor report from the cloud infrastructure provider; monthly internal compliance dashboards showing forced logout, account lock, and chargeback reversal rates; and the Terms of Service explicitly prohibiting sale, transfer, or redemption of in-app credits outside the app. Also submit correspondence with Apple and Google compliance teams confirming that payments are subject to their merchant reviews and refund mechanisms.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return including national corporate income tax and local corporate income tax surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year end, the corporate tax return and payment are due by March 31 of the following year; if a licensed certified tax accountant or CPA prepares the return, the extended due date is April 30 (the last day of the fourth month after fiscal year close).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a 20% non-filing penalty on the tax payable; underreported amounts carry a 10% to 40% understatement penalty depending on willfulness; unpaid tax accrues daily interest at the statutory rate of 0.022% per day on the overdue amount. A continued delinquency after NTS demand results in asset seizure, a written notice of business closure and cancellation of the business registration, and ultimately a court-ordered administrative strike-off/dissolution of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular ordinary general meeting of members and approval of the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ; meeting minutes and resolutions preserved in the statutory minute book at the registered office (no separate government filing is required unless an external audit applies).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) under the Korean Commercial Act, the ordinary general meeting of members must be convened within two months after the close of each fiscal year, i.e., by February 28/29 for a December 31 fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the regular meeting within the two-month window allows any member to petition the court to order convocation. If the LLC does not hold an ordinary meeting for two consecutive fiscal years or remains fully inactive for five years, the court may issue an order of dissolution, which is the administrative trigger for striking the entity from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements filing with the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) - external audit information system (EAISS); also to be tabled at the ordinary general meeting and filed with the Commercial Registry as applicable under the Commercial Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must deliver the audit report at least two weeks before the ordinary general meeting of members; the audited financial statements and audit report must be submitted to the FSS no later than six weeks after the meeting and, in any event, by April 30 for a December fiscal year end where a February meeting cannot be held earlier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo or file the statutory external audit subjects the company to an administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 38,000), referral of the auditor to FSS inspection, and a compulsory external audit order; repeated non-compliance or a misstated audit report is a ground for court-ordered dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final quarterly VAT return for the fourth tax period (October-December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the fourth VAT period return must be filed with the NTS on or before January 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late return adds a 20% unfaithful-return penalty and a daily interest of 0.03% on the overdue VAT amount; failure to issue or maintain valid tax invoices can add 1%-2% penalties on the supply value; persistent VAT default can lead to NTS seizure and administrative closure/cancellation of the business registration, followed by strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payment statement (withholding tax summary) for employees and independent author royalties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 10 of the year following the year in which wages, salaries, or royalty payments were made; for the calendar-year reporting period, the annual statement is due by March 10.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission or omission of a payment statement attracts an additional tax of up to 3% of the unreported or unfaithfully reported amounts; continued failure to file after a demand may result in NTS administrative assessment, business-registration closure, and administrative strike-off after an extended period of inaction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and amendment of the statutory registers, articles of association, member interests and beneficial ownership records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Court registry (Commercial Registration section of the competent District Court) and National Tax Service business registration office for changes in members, directors, or authorized capital.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any transfer of an LLC membership interest, admission or withdrawal of a member, appointment or removal of a director, or amendment to registered articles must be filed with the court registry within 30 days of the event; the member register must be confirmed and closed at the ordinary general meeting each fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registry filing exposes the company to administrative fines of up to KRW 5 million (approximately USD 3,800) under the Commercial Act; inaccurate NTS business-registration changes may produce a 10% corporate-tax understatement penalty and, for severe or malicious non-compliance, the same administrative strike-off mechanism as tax delinquency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is statutorily required to appoint an independent certified public accountant (CPA) if its total assets at the end of the preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million). No separate turnover or employee-headcount trigger applies to a private LLC under the Korean external audit rules for companies not listed and not in the financial sector. However, if the LLC also has characteristics of a public-interest company (e.g., it is listed, operates as a financial company, or has total assets above KRW 50 billion), the audit must be performed under K-IFRS; otherwise, the audit is performed under K-GAAP (local GAAP) or the SME simplified external audit standards, and the CPA must issue an independent opinion on the statement of financial position, statement of profit or loss, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows and notes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for a mandatory-audit company that is publicly listed or that exceeds KRW 50 billion (approx. USD 37.5 million) in total assets; for all other Yuhan Hoesa LLCs, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) / Small and Medium Enterprise Accounting Standards apply for statutory accounting and audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not yet impose a single one-size-fits-all annual UBO declaration for private LLCs. Instead, the Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a correct register of members and update it, together with its registered articles, at the ordinary general meeting each fiscal year. Any equity-interest transfer (sale, inheritance, pledge, or redemption) must be reported to the court registry and the tax authority within 30 days of the change. In parallel, each financial counterparty (including the bank connected to Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payment rails) is required by FATF-aligned Korean financial transaction and AML law to perform customer due diligence and to refresh the beneficial-owner identification at least annually; the company must therefore provide a confirmation of its ultimate beneficial owner and control chain whenever a licensed financial institution makes the annual KYC/AML request. Failure to provide accurate UBO information can subject the company to anti-money-laundering sanctions and transaction blocking, although it is not an automatic corporate strike-off trigger.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 - $1,500 per year for a standard Seoul-region registered-office and corporate secretarial agent package (market range, not a government fee).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 - $20,000 per year for a statutory audit prepared under the SME simplified external audit standards; fees increase to $30,000 - $80,000 or more if K-IFRS, group consolidation, or transfer pricing schedules are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (top marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential free-zone incentives under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, R&D tax credits, foreign-invested high-tech tax holidays, and IP/patent box-style income deductions for eligible patents and utility models

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (beobinsa gwa-se-pyo jeong-san) filed via National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system (HTS)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate tax number (business registration number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must enter the Korean business registration number of the domestic corporation, not the foreign shareholder's ID; attach the Schedule for Foreign Investment if non-resident ownership is declared, and state the foreign shareholding percentage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting revenue and expense adjustments for statutory taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible expenses paid to foreign related parties, including interest, royalties, and management fees; disclose any transfer pricing adjustments in the TP disclosure attachments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after loss carryforward and statutory deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate all tax incentives claimed; for non-resident shareholders, confirm that no treaty-limited deduction is illegally reducing Korean taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the progressive corporate tax schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the headline rate bracket and ensure that branch remittance tax, if this entity operates as a Korean branch, is not double-counted as a dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign income taxes paid abroad
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Foreign Tax Credit form and substantiate the withholding amount; if the foreign jurisdiction is a treaty partner, ensure the credit does not exceed the Korean treaty-rate limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 (Amount of Tax Return and Payment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessed corporate tax liability after credits and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that dividend, interest, and royalty payments to non-residents are separately reported for withholding tax; late payment triggers daily surcharges and statutory interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax under Article 76 of the Corporate Tax Act; additional daily surcharge of 0.06% for late payment; willful evasion triggers criminal penalties of up to twice the evaded tax plus imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% income tax + 2% local income tax surtax) for outbound dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File a written application with the National Tax Service using the non-resident tax exemption/reduction request form, attach a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, provide detailed beneficial ownership declarations, and substantiate that the recipient is the beneficial owner with genuine economic activity and no conduit arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT of 22% (20% + 2% local tax) for royalties and interest; applicable treaty rates typically reduce the rate to 10-15% for interest and 10% for royalties, subject to the same TRC and beneficial ownership procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion in annual cross-border related-party transactions for Local File; Master File required when annual revenue exceeds KRW 50 billion and related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the CFC/GAAR provisions; treaty shopping is restricted by Limitation on Benefits clauses in Korean DTAs, and an entity without Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea may be treated as a conduit and subject to anti-abuse reclassification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Intentional Omission of Foreign-Source Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting web novel subscription revenue from foreign users or routing receipts through shell non-resident accounts to avoid Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: administrative penalty of up to 40% of the evaded tax or 3 times the unpaid amount in certain cases; plus 20% negligence tax under Article 76 of the Corporate Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil joint liability: directors who participated or colluded are personally liable for evaded taxes and penalties; criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years, or up to 10 years for aggravated evasion exceeding KRW 5 billion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a non-resident shareholder holding company with no employees, physical office, or Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, used only to extract dividends at treaty-zero rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 23 of the International Tax Adjustment Act permits denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of the dividends as taxable Korean-sourced income; a surcharge of 30% of the under-withheld tax may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Article 2 of the same act: original shareholders and directors are jointly liable for unpaid Korean tax; directors may also be subject to travel bans and asset seizure orders during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Foreign Exchange Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report large foreign remittances of royalties or dividends and not maintaining beneficial ownership records, enabling anonymous digital-content receipts and profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information: penalty of up to KRW 50 million per unreported remittance and up to 10 years imprisonment for willful AML breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally responsible for AML compliance; violation leads to civil restitution of illicit proceeds, a denial of corporate veil immunity, and criminal imprisonment terms of up to 5 years.
